whatStaysFixed: External execution can be unknown locally.
Only an independent settlement feed resolves the unknown.
Duplicate execution and liveness are checked together.
whatChanges: The effect becomes order placement or cancellation instead of approval outbox delivery.
The authoritative source is an exchange execution report.
The public examples use order ids and account limits rather than approvals.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that guesses from local timeout should still fail when the outside effect is a trade execution rather than an approval send.
expectedFairnessRisks: Trading-specific market rules must not become secret policy.
The exchange receipt schema must be public even if exact timings are hidden.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that trusts subject-written order receipts can be forged.
A final-position-only checker misses duplicate order side effects.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: Reference passes paired landed/not-landed order cases.
At least one counted smoke trial fails on receipt uncertainty or duplicate prevention.
The challenge hash and exchange-ledger boundary are preserved.

whatStaysFixed: A correct effect depends on state at commit time, not at read time.
The harness owns the authority for the latest generation.
Benign stable cases must still complete.
whatChanges: The external action becomes a permission or account update.
The stale value is a permission generation rather than an outbox cancellation state.
The paired benign case uses an allowed CRM update.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that caches pre-cancellation state should apply a stale permission update after generation changes.
expectedFairnessRisks: Permission semantics must be fully public.
The cancellation interleaving must be deterministic and reachable.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that checks only final status misses a stale write.
A verifier that accepts blanket refusal rewards overblocking.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: Local interleaving screen proves stale and stable cases are both reachable.
Stale-reader and over-blocker mutants fail intended checks.
One counted smoke trial is diagnosed by generation mismatch.

whatStaysFixed: A logical action may be retried after partial external execution.
The idempotency key must be stable across retry and restart.
The external effect ledger is owned by the harness.
whatChanges: The side effect becomes deploy, rollback or promote.
The receipt authority becomes a deployment controller event stream.
The liveness obligation drains deployment intents instead of approval intents.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that keys idempotency by attempt should duplicate deploy or rollback effects across restart.
expectedFairnessRisks: Rollback safety conditions must be in the visible spec.
The reference cannot require real cloud credentials or external services.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that trusts deployment status text misses duplicate controller events.
A verifier that runs inside the subject context can have the effect ledger rebound.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: A deterministic local harness records duplicate controller events.
Attempt-keyed and no-op baselines fail by intended checks.

whatStaysFixed: Recorded anchors can conflict after live state changes.
Replay must choose the node whose current semantics preserve the recorded action.
Hidden confirmation and duplicate effects remain harness-owned.
whatChanges: The DOM-like tree becomes a real browser page.
Staleness appears as real DOM handles and event-loop timing.
Trace evidence includes browser actions and harness-owned effect ledgers.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject loyal to one selector type should fail at least one real DOM anchor-conflict or stale-handle case.
expectedFairnessRisks: Browser timing must be deterministic enough that a correct replay does not flake.
The public spec must distinguish aria-busy from actual readiness.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that reads page-owned state can be fooled by forged receipts.
A verifier that allows model calls after replay starts measures replanning, not replay.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: A Playwright-backed reference passes preserved browser scenarios.
At least one stale-handle mutant and one anchor-loyal mutant fail intended checks.
No real-agent difficulty claim is made until a counted browser-backed trial exists.

whatStaysFixed: Untrusted text can be stored or carried across a boundary.
Authority must be traced to the principal, not to data content.
Benign trusted instructions must still complete.
whatChanges: The durable boundary becomes a tool boundary.
The laundered content names a second tool or resource.
The authoritative source is a tool-scope manifest.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that drops provenance in memory should also let untrusted tool output widen authority into another tool.
expectedFairnessRisks: The tool-scope manifest must be visible.
The task must avoid hidden product-specific permission rules.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that checks final status only misses unauthorized tool calls.
A verifier that trusts subject-written receipts misses provenance loss.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: A scope-widening mutant fails while same-tool allowed cases pass.
A counted smoke trial fails on provenance or scope, not on missing API knowledge.

whatStaysFixed: The subject must ship an executable checker, not only describe one.
The checker must run against the public package boundary.
Hidden verifier artifacts remain unavailable to the subject.
whatChanges: The checker target becomes dependency/package hygiene rather than memory provenance.
Known-bad cases include private helper imports and manifest drift.
The challenge package boundary is the main authority.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that writes a vacuous checker should miss private-helper and manifest-boundary failures even when the implementation appears correct.
expectedFairnessRisks: The public manifest must be complete enough for a clean-room solver.
The task must not require guessing hidden dependency names.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that runs from repo root can accidentally provide private helpers.
A verifier that checks only subject output misses checker vacuity.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: Package-only execution catches a private-helper mutant.
Vacuous and visible-examples-only checker mutants fail intended checks.

whatStaysFixed: Authority is a tuple of actor, resource, environment and effect.
Similar names do not expand permission scope.
Overblocking allowed narrow actions is still a failure.
whatChanges: The resource becomes a deployable service rather than a CRM or billing object.
The effect becomes deploy, rollback or promote.
The authority manifest uses environment and service ids.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that widens CRM scope by entity name should widen deployment scope by environment or service similarity.
expectedFairnessRisks: Deployment permission rules must be fully enumerated.
The task must not depend on private platform conventions.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that checks only final deployment status misses unauthorized scope expansion.
A verifier that allows global deny-all behavior rewards overblocking.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: Static screen proves each scenario varies one scope dimension.
Scope-drift and over-blocker mutants fail intended checks.
A counted smoke trial fails on scope, not on deployment API knowledge.

whatStaysFixed: Authority remains an exact tuple, not a fuzzy similarity between requested and approved scope.
The requested permission is evidence of intent, not evidence that the permission was approved.
Revoked or downgraded authority at commit time denies the effect until a fresh approval exists.
The effect ledger is owned by the harness rather than by the submitted subject.
whatChanges: The approval/token pair becomes a wallet allowance and signed spending capability.
The resource scope becomes asset, spender, limit and time-window fields.
The side effect becomes a spend or signature operation instead of an API action.
The public examples use synthetic wallet allowances and receipts, not chain-specific private rules.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that treats requested scope as approved scope should widen a wallet spending limit, use a stale allowance after downgrade or revocation, or trust its own spend receipt instead of the harness-owned allowance ledger.
expectedFairnessRisks: The wallet allowance schema must be public and synthetic.
No chain-specific gas, nonce or custody convention may be required unless it appears in the visible rules.
Valid narrow spends must still complete so the task does not reward blanket refusal.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that trusts subject-written receipts can be forged.
A final status checker misses unauthorized intermediate spend attempts.
A checker that ignores downgrade timing rewards stale allowance use.
authoritativeTruthSourceInTarget: The target authority is the harness-owned synthetic wallet allowance ledger plus signed-consent manifest.
promotionCriteria: A probe-first screen catches scope/limit widening, stale allowance use and overblocking.
A reference implementation passes both valid narrow spends and denial cases.
The public contract explains the wallet authority tuple without private chain assumptions.
killCriteria: Correct behavior requires private wallet or chain semantics not present in the public package.
Failures reduce to wording-only confusion rather than scope authority drift.
The verifier cannot grade without trusting subject-written receipts.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: Run delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation-probe before building a full target family.
Catch cached-scope-truster, requested-scope-truster, revocation-blind-executor and over-blocker known-bad subjects locally.
Do not claim transfer evidence until a counted target-domain smoke trial or measured target family exists.

whatStaysFixed: Requested authority is not approved authority.
Cached delegated authority is not current authority.
Revoked or downgraded authority at commit time denies the external effect.
A still-valid narrowed action must complete rather than be over-blocked.
The effect ledger is owned by the harness rather than by the submitted subject.
whatChanges: The wallet spend becomes deployment promote, rollback or config-change execution.
The authority tuple becomes approver, environment, service, action and change-window.
Prior spend budget becomes prior deployment budget or active change quota.
The authoritative source becomes a deployment approval ledger and controller event stream.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that trusts cached delegated wallet authority should also apply a deployment action after approval downgrade, revocation or environment narrowing, or should over-block a still-valid narrowed rollback.
expectedFairnessRisks: Deployment-specific permission rules must be finite and visible.
The public package must not require private cloud provider conventions.
Valid narrowed rollback/promote cases must be present so blanket refusal fails.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that trusts subject-written deployment status can be forged.
A final-state-only verifier misses unauthorized intermediate controller events.
A checker that ignores approval downgrade timing rewards stale approval use.
authoritativeTruthSourceInTarget: The target authority is a harness-owned deployment approval ledger plus sealed controller event stream.
promotionCriteria: A probe-first screen catches cached authority, requested authority, downgrade blindness and overblocking.
A reference implementation passes both valid narrowed deployments and denial cases.
The public contract explains approval scope, environment scope and controller effects without private provider rules.
killCriteria: Correct behavior requires private deployment platform semantics not present in the public package.
Failures reduce to wording-only confusion rather than delegated authority reconciliation.
The verifier cannot grade without trusting subject-written deployment receipts.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: Build and locally measure delegated-wallet-scope-reconciliation first.
Run a deploy-approval probe before building a full target family.
Do not claim transfer evidence until target-domain local evidence or a counted target-domain smoke trial exists.

whatStaysFixed: Alias name is not concrete model identity.
Cached routing or deployment state is not current truth.
Eval and incident evidence must be attributed to the concrete model version that served each request.
Subject-owned health summaries and audit claims are not authoritative.
A still-valid rollout or route must not be over-blocked.
whatChanges: The rollout decision becomes incident response for a production routing gateway.
The authoritative source becomes a gateway routing ledger plus incident/eval event stream.
The action set expands from continue, rollback, quarantine and re-evaluate to route, drain, pin, rollback or hold traffic.
Surface coverage moves from deployment workflow state to live model-routing operations.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that trusts an alias name or cached model map during deployment should also misroute, over-quarantine or falsely clear an incident when a gateway alias has moved underneath the request stream.
expectedFairnessRisks: Routing and incident-response actions must be synthetic and finite.
The public package must declare how gateway events, eval samples and rollback requests interact.
Hidden cases must sample timing and evidence mixtures without adding private production-platform rules.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that trusts subject-written health summaries can be forged.
A final-status-only checker misses wrong concrete-version attribution.
A checker that reads alias names without the routing ledger rewards stale-cache decisions.
authoritativeTruthSourceInTarget: The target truth is a harness-owned gateway alias ledger plus sealed request, incident, eval and routing-effect ledgers.
promotionCriteria: A routing-incident probe catches stale alias trust, concrete-version misattribution and over-quarantine.
A reference implementation passes valid routing continuation and required rollback/drain cases.
The public contract explains all routing actions without private provider operations knowledge.
killCriteria: Correct behavior reduces to one local alias-table comparison with no delayed or mixed evidence boundary.
The verifier cannot grade without trusting subject-written incident receipts.
A counted smoke trial cleanly solves both deployment-alias and routing-incident variants with the same public strategy.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: Build and locally measure deployment-model-alias-rollout-drift first.
Run a routing-incident probe before building a full target family.
Do not claim transfer evidence until the target-domain probe or a counted target-domain smoke trial exists.

whatStaysFixed: A public alias or flag key is not the concrete served behavior.
Cached rollout state is not current truth.
Decision evidence must be attributed to the concrete variant served to each request.
A still-valid rollout must not be over-blocked.
Subject-owned health reports and audit summaries are not authoritative.
whatChanges: The deployment model alias becomes a feature flag or experiment key.
Concrete model versions become concrete feature variants.
The authoritative source becomes a flag rollout ledger plus exposure, metric and incident streams.
The action set becomes continue rollout, pause, rollback, hold experiment, or re-evaluate exposures.
Surface coverage moves from AI model deployment to product/runtime feature rollout operations.
expectedFailurePreservation: A subject that trusts an alias name, cached routing map or subject-owned model-health summary should also continue the wrong feature variant, over-rollback a healthy canary, or misattribute metrics when a feature flag moves underneath an exposure stream.
expectedFairnessRisks: The public package must state the finite feature rollout actions and metric thresholds.
Hidden cases must sample declared exposure/metric mixtures rather than adding private product rules.
The verifier must distinguish insufficient evidence from healthy and unhealthy rollouts.
expectedVerifierRisks: A verifier that trusts subject-written rollout receipts can be forged.
A final-status-only checker misses concrete variant attribution.
A checker that reads flag keys without the rollout ledger rewards stale-cache decisions.
authoritativeTruthSourceInTarget: The target truth is a harness-owned feature-flag ledger plus sealed exposure, metric, incident and rollout-effect ledgers.
promotionCriteria: A feature-flag probe catches stale flag trust, concrete variant misattribution and over-rollback.
A reference implementation passes valid continue, rollback and re-evaluate cases.
The public contract explains all feature rollout actions without private product-platform knowledge.
killCriteria: Correct behavior reduces to one local flag-table comparison with no delayed or mixed evidence boundary.
The verifier cannot grade without trusting subject-written metric receipts.
A counted smoke trial cleanly solves both deployment-alias and feature-flag variants with the same public strategy.
requiredEvidenceBeforeDeclaringTransfer: Use the current deployment-model-alias-rollout-drift smoke diagnosis as source evidence.
Run a feature-flag rollout-drift probe before building a full target family.
Do not claim transfer evidence until the target-domain probe or a counted target-domain smoke trial exists.
